**h01.** `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16`, work in `CheckAndPresign` at `:47`) — refreshes S3 presigned URLs for attachments whose `LastPresignedTime` is older than 4 days (URLs expire at 5 days).
**Schedule:** once synchronously at startup, then every 12 hours (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`; ticker loop `:31-40`).
**Wiring:** `Server.startBackgroundRunners` — `server/server.go:162` (construct), `server/server.go:163` (`RunOnce`), `server/server.go:169` (`Run` goroutine), called from `Server.Start` at `server/server.go:129`.

**h02.** Delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`; the actual HTTP call is `safeClient.Do(req)` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`. It runs on 4 worker goroutines draining `asyncPostQueue` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39-55`), fed by `PostAsync` (`:184`).
Protection (SSRF, two layers):
- Dial-time: `safeClient`'s transport uses `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:29-37`, `:59-77`), which resolves the host and rejects reserved/private IPs via `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:240`) against `reservedCIDRs` (loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254.0.0/16 IMDS, IPv6 equivalents — `internal/webhook/validate.go:210-219`). This also defeats DNS rebinding.
- Config-time: `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:258`) enforces http/https + non-reserved IP when webhooks are created/updated (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`).
- Escape hatch: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:237`), set from the `--allow-private-webhooks` flag (`cmd/memos/main.go:47`).

**h03.** Abstraction package: `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go:1` — `IdentityProviderUserInfo`, the common user-info contract). Implementation package: `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:2`, `IdentityProvider` / `NewIdentityProvider` at `:20,:27`). OAuth2 is the only concrete protocol implementation that ships.

**h04.** **No.** `mysql.NewDB` is referenced in exactly one place: the factory `db.NewDBDriver` at `store/db/db.go:22`. A repo-wide grep for `mysql.NewDB(` / `mysql.DB{` yields only that line (tests construct `sqlite.NewDB` instead — `store/demo_seed_test.go:24`, `store/deployment_config_test.go:416`). Everything else reaches MySQL through the `store.Driver` interface (`store/driver.go`).

ON DELETE CASCADE` in the schemas is on `memo_share.memo_id` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109`, `postgres/LATEST.sql:108`, `mysql/LATEST.sql:108`).

**r01.** Premise is wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in this repo (no `redis` match in any `.go` file or in `go.mod`). Caching is an in-process, in-memory cache: `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache`, `New` at `:76`). The store creates three of them — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — in `store.New` (`store/store.go:26-28`, `:48-50`) with `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5m`, `MaxItems: 1000` (`store/store.go:39-43`; same defaults in `store/cache/cache.go:59`). So user entries expire after **10 minutes**, and are also invalidated explicitly on delete (`store/user_delete.go:39-47`).

**r02.** Premise is wrong: there is no rate-limiting middleware in this codebase — no per-user or global rate limiter is registered. Grep for `ratelimit`/`rate_limit` finds only a comment in `internal/email/doc.go:86` listing it as a suggested practice. The Echo middleware actually registered is only `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`, `server/cors.go`); the API v1 chain adds auth/authorization interceptors (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:66+`, `connect_interceptors.go`, `authz.go`), not rate limiting. The nearest concurrency controls are semaphores for thumbnail/image work (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:57-58`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:107`).

**r03.** Premise is wrong: no nightly database-cleanup job is scheduled, and no cron scheduler is running. `internal/scheduler` exists as a standalone, unused library — its only importers are its own tests (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10`, `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`). The `"0 2 * * *"` "daily-cleanup" is just a doc-comment example (`internal/scheduler/doc.go:14-21`), not a registered job. The only background work the server actually starts is the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour `time.Ticker` (`server/server.go:153-174`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`).

**r04.** Premise is wrong: there is no message broker at all — no NATS, RabbitMQ, AMQP, or Kafka in the code or `go.mod`, and no queue is declared anywhere externally. Webhook delivery uses an in-process buffered Go channel: `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`), drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`) calling `Post` (`:120`). Producers call `PostAsync` (`:184`), which drops the payload with a warning when the buffer is full. It is not durable — pending payloads are lost on restart.

**r05.** Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL schema or GraphQL server in this repo (no `graphql` match in Go sources or `go.mod`). The public API is gRPC/Protobuf defined under `proto/api/v1/*.proto`, generated into `proto/gen/api/v1/`, and exposed over HTTP three ways: gRPC-Gateway REST (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go` `RegisterGateway`, `proto/gen/api/v1/*.pb.gw.go`), Connect RPC handlers (`server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go`, `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/`), plus an OpenAPI document (`proto/openapi_embed.go`) and an MCP surface (`server/router/mcp/`). Non-RPC HTTP surfaces are the file server (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`) and RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`).
